P.text: In AtomWallet._validateSignature, after ECDSA.tryRecover, the InvalidSignatureS branch is reached when the s component of a signature is in the upper half of the secp256k1 curve order (high-s signature); a high-s counterpart can be derived from any observed valid owner signature via s' = curve_order - s with identical recovered address.
P.evidence_quote: `RecoverError.InvalidSignatureS` is triggered by OpenZeppelin's ECDSA library when the `s` component of a signature falls in the upper half of the secp256k1 curve order (high-s signature).

I.text: ERC-4337 requires validateUserOp to validate the signature of the userOpHash and SHOULD return SIG_VALIDATION_FAILED (1) without reverting on signature mismatch; the InvalidSignature branch returns _packValidationData(true, ...) (SIG_VALIDATION_FAILED).
I.evidence_quote: "MUST validate that the signature is a valid signature of the userOpHash, and SHOULD return SIG_VALIDATION_FAILED (1) without reverting on signature mismatch."

V.text: The InvalidSignatureS branch unconditionally reverts instead of returning SIG_VALIDATION_FAILED, so validateUserOp reverts; during on-chain handleOps the EntryPoint calls validateUserOp without try/catch and the revert propagates through the entire bundle, causing the bundler's transaction to fail, and enabling adversary-constructable griefing, bundler availability disruption, and wallet degradation.
V.evidence_quote: However, the `InvalidSignatureS` branch unconditionally reverts instead.
